subject: Request: Hosted API latency addendum & measurement playbook
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <ops@novacare.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rebecca Lin <procurement@novacare.com>
Date: 2026-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API latency addendum request

Connor,

Thanks for the ongoing support — we really like Redwood's performance so far. As we move to finalize the enterprise agreement (NC-2026-042) Procurement asked us to lock down explicit latency commitments for the Hosted API (p50/p95) and clarify how you measure those numbers. Two specific asks from NovaCare: 

- Can Redwood commit to p50 and p95 targets for our account (examples below) with a 30-day rolling measurement window instead of the standard 7-day window?
  - Target suggestion: p50 <= 70ms, p95 <= 320ms (business critical paths)
- Define carve-outs and measurement rules (business hours vs all-hours, maintenance windows, regional failovers).

I attached a CSV showing our observed p95 trend over Q1 to give context (novacare_p95_trend_Q1_2026.csv). Rebecca (procurement) is copied — they prefer commitments in an addendum we can attach to the Master Services Agreement.

Can you advise next steps and whether Redwood can provide a formal addendum + playbook for measuring and reporting? We need this to close by the end of March.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform Operations
NovaCare

--- Attachment: novacare_p95_trend_Q1_2026.csv (CSV, 42KB)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <ops@novacare.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency addendum request

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the clear note and the CSV, that helps. We can support a formal addendum; propose the following immediate next steps so Procurement has what they need quickly:

1) Redwood drafts an SLO addendum (initial version attached: proposed_slo_addendum_v1.docx) that uses a 30-day rolling measurement window and enumerates carve-outs for scheduled maintenance and catastrophic regional outages.
2) Marissa (CS) will own the commercial compromise (specific targets and credits).
3) Karthik (SRE/Product) will confirm the measurement methodology (what counts as a valid sample, how we treat cold starts / KV cache effects, success vs error responses).
4) We run a 30-day canary on NovaCare routes if you want an observational period before signing; results feed into the final addendum.

Initial take: we can probably commit to a p50 <= 75ms and p95 <= 350ms across your primary region with business-hours measurement (09:00-17:00 local) and a 30-day rolling window, subject to a few clarifications: sample size floor, definition of business-hours, and agreed carve-outs. Marissa — can you propose the commercial parameters (credit bands, review cadence)? Karthik — can you confirm the technical measurement rules and minimum sample size?

Sanjay — Rebecca, if Procurement has a template addendum they prefer, send it over and we'll align. I'll kick off the draft today and share the playbook (metrics + queries + reporting) so NovaCare's SREs can validate.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0142

--- Attachment: proposed_slo_addendum_v1.docx (DOCX, 28KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <ops@novacare.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rebecca Lin <procurement@novacare.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-16T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency addendum request — commercial proposal

Hi all — following Connor's note, here is a commercial proposal to get Procurement moving while Karthik finalizes measurement rules:

- Proposed committed targets (account-level): p50 <= 70ms, p95 <= 320ms measured over a 30-day rolling window during business hours (09:00–17:00 PT).
- Measurement buckets: business-hours (primary), all-hours (informational only).
- Sample floor: at least 100k successful requests in a 30-day window to qualify for credit. If sample floor not met, we fall back to a 90-day review period for SLA calculations.
- Carve-outs: scheduled maintenance (>=72 hours notice), force majeure, and region-wide cloud provider outages recorded by public status pages.
- Credits: tiered credits at 10% increments for p95 breaches beyond a defined threshold; detailed table in the addendum.
- Review cadence: quarterly SLA review and one technical audit within first 90 days after signing.

We can accept a 30-day observational canary where Redwood mirrors measurement but the final commitment goes into effect after the canary and a joint sign-off. I attached a short measurements playbook (measurements_playbook_v0.3.pdf) that outlines the queries and dashboards we'll use for reporting.

Procurement / Rebecca — does this structure align with NovaCare's approval flow? If so, Connor and I will work with Legal to convert to binding language and route through DocuSign.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference

--- Attachment: measurements_playbook_v0.3.pdf (PDF, 55KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <ops@novacare.com>, Rebecca Lin <procurement@novacare.com>
Date: 2026-03-18T14:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency addendum request — measurement rules (technical)

Connor / Marissa / Sanjay — technical clarifications from SRE side to finalize the playbook and addendum language:

- Measurement definition: p50 and p95 computed from server-side inbound request completion times for successful generation responses (HTTP 2xx). We exclude client-side timeouts and 5xx errors from latency distribution; separate error SLA applies.
- Windowing: rolling 30-day window, advanced by 1 hour buckets. Business-hours filter applies to request timestamp in the customer's primary region (we'll map NovaCare's timezone to PT as discussed).
- Sample floor: 100k successful requests per 30-day window to be eligible for credit. If below floor, the 30-day window is treated as advisory and we use a rolling 90-day review for escalations.
- Cold-start / KV cache: cold-starts are included in measurement; however, we will provide an appendix with warm-vs-cold breakdown for diagnostics and exclude automated model roll restarts (maintenance) when documented.
- Regional aggregation: SLOs apply to the customer's pinned region. Cross-region failover events that result in >10% traffic shift for >10 minutes are eligible for carve-out after joint investigation.
- Reporting: Redwood will provide daily exported metrics (CSV) and a weekly SLO dashboard snapshot. The DocuSign addendum will reference the dashboard queries (we'll include the exact PromQL/SQL snippets in the playbook).

Action items: Connor — open a procurement ticket and confirm whether NovaCare wants the 30-day observational canary before or after signing. Marissa — I'll embed the measurement queries into the next addendum draft. Legal — will route DocuSign once Procurement confirms.

If you prefer, we can run the observational canary now for 30 days and sign an implementation addendum after we confirm numbers. That gives both sides confidence before an enforceable credit schedule is attached.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE | Redwood Inference
